THE YMCA YEAR BOOK ON THE INTERNET ARCHIVE — A COMPLETE INVENTORY
==================================================================
Compiled 2026-09-06 (p_436). This file exists so that nobody enumerates this series again.

WHY IT WAS NEEDED
-----------------
Four separate things were wrong with how this project had been finding volumes in this series.

1. THE ENUMERATION WAS TOO NARROW. `identifier:ymcayearbookoffi*` returns three items. The series
   is also catalogued under `ymcayearbookand*`, `yearbookofyoungm*` and `yearbookyoungme*`, and
   under a second title, "Year Book of the Young Men's Christian Associations of North America".

2. THE SCRAPE ENDPOINT WAS SERVING STALE RESULTS. See f_4978. Use advancedsearch.php with
   output=json, and keep a control query whose answer you already know.

3. THE CATALOGUE YEARS ARE UNRELIABLE, AND NOT BY A LITTLE. ymcayearbookand00amergoog is
   catalogued 1907 and is the 1909 volume. Others are catalogued by the FIRST of several volumes
   bound into the same scan.

4. SCANS HOLD MULTIPLE VOLUMES. Six of the thirteen items do. One holds five.

And the sweep built to correct point 4 had its own hole: it matched "FOR THE YEAR NNNN" and so
missed the 1909 volume, which dates itself "May 1, 1908, to April 30, 1909", and missed the 1882
volume, whose OCR reads "FOB THE YEAR". EVERY PATTERN USED HERE FAILED AT LEAST ONCE. The
inventory below was finished by reading front matter directly wherever a pattern returned nothing.

TELLING A TITLE PAGE FROM A STATISTICS HEADING, since both read "FOR THE YEAR NNNN": a title page
sits under "UNITED STATES AND DOMINION OF CANADA" or "NORTH AMERICA," and above a price line
("Price, 50 Cents"); a statistics heading names the PREVIOUS year and follows a line about
American associations.


THE INVENTORY
-------------
Item                          Volumes it contains          Catalogued as
----------------------------  ---------------------------  -------------
yearbookofyoungm00youn        1881-82                      1881
ymcayearbookand01amergoog     1882(-83?), 1884             1882
ymcayearbookand02amergoog     1886, 1887, 1888, 1890       1886
yearbookofyoungm0000vari      1891, 1892                   (none)
ymcayearbookand02assogoog     1891, 1892, 1893, 1894, 1895 1891   [in order — see below]
ymcayearbookand00assogoog     1896, 1897, 1898, 1899, 1900 1896
yearbookyoungme01commgoog     1899, 1900                   1899
ymcayearbookand00amergoog     1909                         1907   [WRONG BY TWO YEARS]
ymcayearbookand01assogoog     1921                         1921
yearbookyoungme00commgoog     1921                         1921
ymcayearbookoffi00youn        1921                         1921
ymcayearbookoffi01youn        1922                         1922
ymcayearbookoffi0000unse      1936                         (none)  [LENDING-RESTRICTED]

Held separately in this project's cache from earlier work: 1893, 1894, 1895, 1896, 1897, 1906,
1907, 1908.

The 1882(-83?) reading is the one soft entry above: its OCR gives "FOB THE YEAR 1882-1888", where
the trailing figure is almost certainly 1883 misread. It is written with the question mark it
deserves.

[CORRECTED 2026-09-06, within the hour. The table first read "ymcayearbookand02assogoog  1891,
1892, 1898, 1894, 1895 ... [bound OUT OF ORDER]". THE THIRD VOLUME IS 1893, NOT 1898. Its title
page is OCR'd "FOR THE YEAR 1898" and its contents are all 1892 and early 1893 — "the year
closing March 1, 1893", "Since April 1, 1892", "The year 1892 witnessed great advance". The scan
is in order; nothing is out of sequence, and the whole "bound out of order" observation was a
misread digit. THESE SCANS CONFUSE 3 AND 8 ROUTINELY — the same OCR gives F. S. Morrison's year
of entry, 93, as "SS".

SO THE RULE HAS A THIRD TERM. A catalogue year is worthless; a title page beats it; AND A
VOLUME'S OWN CONTENTS BEAT ITS TITLE PAGE'S OCR. Where two items hold the same year, read both —
the disagreement between them is what exposed this one. (The 1898 volume in
ymcayearbookand00assogoog is genuinely 1898: its text refers to "the beginning of the year 1898",
and the Archibald McKellar reading taken from it stands.)]


SO THE SERIES IS AVAILABLE FOR:
  1881-82, 1884, 1886, 1887, 1888, 1890, 1891, 1892, 1893, 1894, 1895, 1896, 1897, 1898,
  1899, 1900, 1906, 1907, 1908, 1909, 1921, 1922, and 1936 (restricted).

AND IT IS NOT AVAILABLE, ANYWHERE ON THE INTERNET ARCHIVE, FOR:
  1883, 1885, 1889, **1901 THROUGH 1905**, **1910 THROUGH 1920**, and 1923 through 1935.

THOSE ARE THE REAL HOLES AND THEY ARE NOT AN ARTEFACT OF A BAD QUERY — this inventory is what
four corrected search methods converge on. 1910-1920 is the one that costs this project most: it
covers the new site's first decade, the whole of the First World War, and the years in which
W. J. Holliday either did or did not get the Boys' Work directorship back. Chase those years at
HathiTrust, Google Books full view, and the Kautz Family YMCA Archives at the University of
Minnesota, which holds the series in print. Not on the Internet Archive.


WHAT THE PRE-CAMP VOLUMES GAVE, AND WHAT THEY DID NOT
-----------------------------------------------------
The 1880s volumes were searched for the camp's people. Read as a null with one exception.

W. H. BALL IS NOT IN ANY OF THEM. He entered Association work in 1889 (f_4976), and the 1892
volume introduces him at Montreal as "the physical director, W. H. Ball Jr., a new man, from the
Springfield Training School". The 1884, 1886, 1887, 1888 and 1890 volumes contain no W. H. Ball
at Montreal or anywhere else. The Balls in them are other men — J. R. Ball, J. J. Ball, John T.
Ball of Meridian, G. L. Ball of Seaforth, B. F. Ball of Boston, J. B. Ball of Sherbrooke, Willard
D. Ball of Los Angeles. THE THREE YEARS BETWEEN HIS ENTRY INTO ASSOCIATION WORK AND HIS ARRIVAL
IN MONTREAL REMAIN BLANK, and this series does not fill them. (The pattern used was run as a
control against two volumes where he IS present before the null was recorded.)

TWO PRE-CAMP MONTREAL NAMES, both checked by grep against the repo and its cache first:

  CHARLES CUSHING, Montreal — the corresponding member FOR QUEBEC in the 1887 volume:
      "Quebec ........ Charlbs Cushino ....Montreal."
  The name occurs NOWHERE in this project. It matters because the Cushings are already tangled in
  the founding: Lemuel Cushing took boys to Lake Saint-Joseph in 1892, W. E. Cushing sat on the
  1892 committee, and Percy H. Cushing was the association's Assistant Secretary in 1894 and 1895.
  A Cushing holding the YMCA's senior Quebec volunteer post five years before any of that is a
  thread worth pulling. IT IS A NAME AND A POST AND NOTHING MORE — no relationship to any other
  Cushing is established here, and none should be assumed from a surname that is not rare.

  G. A. KUHRING, Assistant at Montreal under D. A. Budge, in the earlier volume of
  ymcayearbookand01amergoog (1882 or 1884 — the line sits before that scan's 1884 title page).
  Also new to this project. The year is left as a range because the scan's first title page could
  not be read cleanly.

In the 1886 volume the Quebec corresponding member is D. A. BUDGE himself, so Cushing succeeded
him — or they alternated — between 1886 and 1887.

QUERIES RUN: advancedsearch.php title queries on both series titles; archive.org/metadata on
every item; /FOR (THE )?YEARS? 1[89]dd/ and /(MAY|APRIL|JAN) 1?[.,]? 1[89]dd,? TO/ across all
thirteen downloaded texts; direct front-matter reads on the items both patterns missed;
/B[ai][Ull]{2}[.,]? W.? H/ across the pre-camp volumes with a control on two volumes where Ball
is known present; 'Montr[a-z]{2,6}' across the pre-camp volumes; and repo-wide greps on
"Charles Cushing", "Chas. Cushing" and "Kuhring".
